paragraphs.title: Keeping the Laws and Living

easy.question: What does Moses command Israel to listen to?
answers: The statutes and judgments
The stories of the patriarchs
The customs of the nations
easy.explanation: Moses tells Israel to listen to the statutes and judgments he teaches them.

easy.question: What will happen if Israel keeps and follows the statutes and judgments?
answers: They will return to Egypt
They will live and possess the land
They will conquer other countries
easy.explanation: The passage says that obeying the laws will enable Israel to live and possess the land.

easy.question: Who is described as being alive to this day?
answers: Those who followed Baal-peor
Only Israel’s leaders
Those who cling to the Lord their God
easy.explanation: Those who cling to the Lord are described as alive, every one of them, to this day.

medium.question: What is the connection between keeping the laws and possessing the land?
answers: Keeping the laws prevents entry into the land
Keeping the laws leads to life and possession of the land
Keeping the laws matters only after the land is possessed
medium.explanation: The passage connects obedience with living and possessing the land.

medium.question: In the phrase “neither shall ye diminish ought from it,” what does “diminish” mean?
answers: Do not add new things
Do not forget the words
Do not remove or take anything away
medium.explanation: The verse contrasts diminishing with adding, so it means not reducing or omitting anything.

medium.question: What happened to those who followed Baal-peor?
answers: The Lord destroyed them from among Israel
They received the land
They became leaders of Israel
medium.explanation: The passage says that the Lord destroyed everyone who followed Baal-peor.

challenge.question: What central contrast appears in verses 3–4?
answers: Those who followed Baal-peor died, while those who clung to the Lord lived
Those who followed Baal-peor possessed the land, while those who clung to the Lord were expelled
Those who followed Baal-peor taught the people, while those who clung to the Lord remained silent
challenge.explanation: The verses contrast the destruction of Baal-peor’s followers with the life of those who clung to the Lord.

challenge.question: Why does Moses emphasize that “your eyes have seen” what happened at Baal-peor?
answers: To describe the beauty of the place
To stress that Israel witnessed it and should learn from it
To say that only children saw it
challenge.explanation: Israel saw the consequences themselves, making the warning especially powerful.

challenge.question: What does the word “every one” emphasize in “are alive every one of you this day”?
answers: Life is not limited to the leaders
Only the priests survived
Everyone in the world is alive at the same time
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that all Israelites who clung to the Lord were alive, not merely a small group.

questions.question: What central contrast appears in verses 3–4?
answers: Those who followed Baal-peor died, while those who clung to the Lord lived
Those who followed Baal-peor possessed the land, while those who clung to the Lord were expelled
Those who followed Baal-peor taught the people, while those who clung to the Lord remained silent
questions.explanation: The verses contrast the destruction of Baal-peor’s followers with the life of those who clung to the Lord.

questions.question: Why does Moses emphasize that “your eyes have seen” what happened at Baal-peor?
answers: To describe the beauty of the place
To stress that Israel witnessed it and should learn from it
To say that only children saw it
questions.explanation: Israel saw the consequences themselves, making the warning especially powerful.

questions.question: What does the word “every one” emphasize in “are alive every one of you this day”?
answers: Life is not limited to the leaders
Only the priests survived
Everyone in the world is alive at the same time
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that all Israelites who clung to the Lord were alive, not merely a small group.

paragraphs.title: Israel’s Laws as Wisdom Before the Nations

easy.question: What did Moses teach the Israelites?
answers: Statutes and judgments
Stories of wars
The names of nations
easy.explanation: Moses says that he taught Israel statutes and judgments.

easy.question: What were the Israelites commanded to do with the statutes and judgments?
answers: Change them
Keep and follow them
Teach them only to the priests
easy.explanation: The passage commands Israel to keep and follow the laws.

easy.question: What would the nations say when they heard these laws?
answers: Israel is a small people
Israel is a distant people
Israel is a wise and understanding people
easy.explanation: The nations would recognize Israel as a wise and understanding people.

medium.question: Why was it important for Israel to keep and follow the statutes and judgments?
answers: The nations would see Israel’s wisdom and understanding
Israel would not need to enter the land
Israel could abolish the Torah
medium.explanation: Obedience would show the nations Israel’s wisdom and understanding.

medium.question: What sequence is described in these verses?
answers: The nations praise Israel, and then Moses teaches the laws
Moses teaches, Israel keeps and follows, and the nations hear and praise
Israel leaves the land, and then receives the laws
medium.explanation: Moses teaches the laws, Israel is to obey them, and the nations then recognize their wisdom.

medium.question: In the phrase “the land whither ye go to possess it,” what does “possess” mean?
answers: Leave it
Hide it
Receive it and take possession of it
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to entering the land in order to receive and possess it.

challenge.question: What two things do verses 7–8 present as evidence of Israel’s greatness?
answers: A near God and righteous statutes and judgments
A large land but no laws
A stronger army than every nation
challenge.explanation: The verses mention the Lord’s nearness and Israel’s righteous laws.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “in the sight of the nations” imply?
answers: The laws were only for Israel’s leaders
Keeping the laws would publicly display Israel’s wisdom to other nations
The nations would determine Israel’s laws
challenge.explanation: Israel’s obedience would be visible and would influence how other nations viewed them.

challenge.question: What does “which I set before you this day” emphasize?
answers: The laws belong only to the past
The laws will be given only after entering the land
The teaching is being presented to Israel now
challenge.explanation: “This day” emphasizes the present time, while “before you” presents the laws as currently placed before Israel.

questions.question: What two things do verses 7–8 present as evidence of Israel’s greatness?
answers: A near God and righteous statutes and judgments
A large land but no laws
A stronger army than every nation
questions.explanation: The verses mention the Lord’s nearness and Israel’s righteous laws.

questions.question: What does the phrase “in the sight of the nations” imply?
answers: The laws were only for Israel’s leaders
Keeping the laws would publicly display Israel’s wisdom to other nations
The nations would determine Israel’s laws
questions.explanation: Israel’s obedience would be visible and would influence how other nations viewed them.

questions.question: What does “which I set before you this day” emphasize?
answers: The laws belong only to the past
The laws will be given only after entering the land
The teaching is being presented to Israel now
questions.explanation: “This day” emphasizes the present time, while “before you” presents the laws as currently placed before Israel.

paragraphs.title: Remembering and Passing on the Torah

easy.question: What does the passage warn people not to do?
answers: Forget what they have seen
Leave the land
Eat before prayer
easy.explanation: The passage warns Israel not to forget what their eyes have seen.

easy.question: To whom were they to teach these things?
answers: Only their friends
Their children and grandchildren
Only the elders
easy.explanation: They were commanded to make these things known to their children and grandchildren.

easy.question: Where did the people stand before the Lord?
answers: Jerusalem
Egypt
Horeb
easy.explanation: The passage recalls the day Israel stood before the Lord at Horeb.

medium.question: Why were the people to keep these things in their hearts all their lives?
answers: So they would not forget and could teach future generations
So they could hide them from the people
So they would not need to learn anything new
medium.explanation: Remembering the teaching would prevent forgetfulness and enable its transmission to later generations.

medium.question: In the phrase “Gather me the people together,” what does “gather” mean?
answers: Scatter the people
Assemble the people
Protect the people
medium.explanation: The command means to bring the people together so they can hear the Lord’s words.

medium.question: What sequence is described?
answers: The people taught their children and then came to Horeb
The people forgot, and then the Lord gathered them
The people stood before the Lord, were gathered, and heard and learned
medium.explanation: The passage recalls Israel at Horeb, the command to gather them, and their hearing and learning.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “Only take heed to thyself, and keep thy soul diligently”?
answers: Remembering requires responsibility and continual effort
It is enough to remember once
The command concerns only physical protection
challenge.explanation: The repeated warning and the word “diligently” call for persistent care and remembrance.

challenge.question: Why does the passage specifically mention the day at Horeb?
answers: To describe a journey through the wilderness
To connect the command with the revelation where Israel heard the Lord
To explain how the city of Horeb was built
challenge.explanation: Horeb links the duty to remember and teach with the revelation Israel experienced there.

challenge.question: What idea is expressed by moving from children to grandchildren?
answers: Each generation should learn only for itself
The teaching was only for the generation at Horeb
Tradition and reverence should continue from generation to generation
challenge.explanation: The command extends teaching beyond one generation, ensuring that it continues into the future.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “Only take heed to thyself, and keep thy soul diligently”?
answers: Remembering requires responsibility and continual effort
It is enough to remember once
The command concerns only physical protection
questions.explanation: The repeated warning and the word “diligently” call for persistent care and remembrance.

questions.question: Why does the passage specifically mention the day at Horeb?
answers: To describe a journey through the wilderness
To connect the command with the revelation where Israel heard the Lord
To explain how the city of Horeb was built
questions.explanation: Horeb links the duty to remember and teach with the revelation Israel experienced there.

questions.question: What idea is expressed by moving from children to grandchildren?
answers: Each generation should learn only for itself
The teaching was only for the generation at Horeb
Tradition and reverence should continue from generation to generation
questions.explanation: The command extends teaching beyond one generation, ensuring that it continues into the future.

paragraphs.title: Mount Sinai and Receiving the Covenant

easy.question: What was happening to the mountain when Israel stood beneath it?
answers: It was burning with fire
It was covered with snow
It was merely quiet and dark
easy.explanation: The mountain burned with fire, while darkness, clouds, and thick darkness surrounded it.

easy.question: What did Israel hear from the fire?
answers: The appearance of an angel
The voice of words
Only the sound of a trumpet
easy.explanation: Israel heard a voice speaking words but saw no form.

easy.question: What were the Ten Commandments written on?
answers: A Torah scroll
One wooden tablet
Two tablets of stone
easy.explanation: The commandments were written on two tablets of stone.

medium.question: What happened after Israel came near and stood beneath the mountain?
answers: They immediately entered the land
The Lord spoke to them from the fire
Moses wrote the judgments alone
medium.explanation: The Lord spoke to Israel from the midst of the fire.

medium.question: In the phrase “darkness, clouds, and thick darkness,” what is “thick darkness”?
answers: Bright light
A loud noise
Dense mist or darkness
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a dense, obscured atmosphere.

medium.question: Why was Moses commanded to teach the people statutes and judgments?
answers: So they could follow them in the land they were entering
So they would remember the names of the mountains
So they could teach only the priests
medium.explanation: The laws were to prepare Israel to live according to them in the land.

challenge.question: What unusual detail appears in the description of the revelation?
answers: Israel saw a clear image of the Lord
Israel heard a voice but saw no form
Israel neither heard nor saw anything
challenge.explanation: The passage stresses that Israel heard words but saw no visible form.

challenge.question: What relationship is shown between the Ten Commandments and the statutes and judgments?
answers: Both merely describe Mount Sinai
The statutes and judgments replaced the Ten Commandments
The Ten Commandments formed part of the covenant, and Moses also taught laws for life in the land
challenge.explanation: The covenant included the Ten Commandments, while Moses was also instructed to teach the laws Israel would keep in the land.

challenge.question: What does “unto the midst of heaven” emphasize about the fire?
answers: Its enormous height and intensity
That it was small and low
That it was located only inside heaven
challenge.explanation: The phrase is vivid language describing a huge, towering fire.

questions.question: What unusual detail appears in the description of the revelation?
answers: Israel saw a clear image of the Lord
Israel heard a voice but saw no form
Israel neither heard nor saw anything
questions.explanation: The passage stresses that Israel heard words but saw no visible form.

questions.question: What relationship is shown between the Ten Commandments and the statutes and judgments?
answers: Both merely describe Mount Sinai
The statutes and judgments replaced the Ten Commandments
The Ten Commandments formed part of the covenant, and Moses also taught laws for life in the land
questions.explanation: The covenant included the Ten Commandments, while Moses was also instructed to teach the laws Israel would keep in the land.

questions.question: What does “unto the midst of heaven” emphasize about the fire?
answers: Its enormous height and intensity
That it was small and low
That it was located only inside heaven
questions.explanation: The phrase is vivid language describing a huge, towering fire.

paragraphs.title: Warning Against Images and Worship of the Heavens

easy.question: Why did Moses command the people to be very careful?
answers: They had seen no form when the Lord spoke to them
They had to build the tabernacle
They did not know the names of the stars
easy.explanation: Israel heard the Lord from the fire but saw no visible form.

easy.question: Which heavenly bodies are mentioned?
answers: Clouds, wind, and rain
The sun, moon, and stars
Mountains, fire, and water
easy.explanation: The passage specifically names the sun, moon, and stars.

easy.question: What were the people warned not to make?
answers: A carved image or likeness of any creature
An altar of stones
A tent in the wilderness
easy.explanation: The passage forbids making images resembling people, animals, birds, fish, or other creatures.

medium.question: In “lest ye corrupt yourselves,” what does “lest” mean?
answers: Perhaps
So that you do not
Immediately
medium.explanation: “Lest” introduces a warning against an undesirable result.

medium.question: How does not seeing a form relate to the prohibition against making an image?
answers: Israel was not given a visible form of the Lord to copy
Israel was allowed to make any image of the Lord
Israel was commanded to draw only the fire
medium.explanation: Because Israel saw no form when the Lord spoke, they had no divine image to imitate.

medium.question: Which kinds of creatures are included in the forbidden likenesses?
answers: Only people and animals
Only birds and fish
Animals, birds, creeping things, and fish
medium.explanation: The list includes creatures on land, in the air, on the ground, and in the water.

challenge.question: What practical danger is described when a person lifts his eyes toward heaven?
answers: He will study the movements of the stars
He may be drawn to worship the sun, moon, and stars
He will find a new place to live
challenge.explanation: The passage describes seeing the heavenly bodies and being drawn to worship and serve them.

challenge.question: What does “all the host of heaven” emphasize?
answers: There is only one star
The heavenly bodies are viewed as a large, ordered group
The heavens are made of human beings
challenge.explanation: “Host” refers collectively to the sun, moon, stars, and other heavenly bodies.

challenge.question: Why does the list include creatures on land, in the sky, and in the water?
answers: To emphasize that no creature may be represented in an image
To select only the most important animals
To teach how to raise animals
challenge.explanation: The broad list shows that the prohibition applies to every kind of created being.

questions.question: What practical danger is described when a person lifts his eyes toward heaven?
answers: He will study the movements of the stars
He may be drawn to worship the sun, moon, and stars
He will find a new place to live
questions.explanation: The passage describes seeing the heavenly bodies and being drawn to worship and serve them.

questions.question: What does “all the host of heaven” emphasize?
answers: There is only one star
The heavenly bodies are viewed as a large, ordered group
The heavens are made of human beings
questions.explanation: “Host” refers collectively to the sun, moon, stars, and other heavenly bodies.

questions.question: Why does the list include creatures on land, in the sky, and in the water?
answers: To emphasize that no creature may be represented in an image
To select only the most important animals
To teach how to raise animals
questions.explanation: The broad list shows that the prohibition applies to every kind of created being.

paragraphs.title: A Treasured People and Covenant Responsibility

easy.question: From where did the Lord bring Israel out?
answers: Egypt
Babylon
Canaan
easy.explanation: The Lord brought Israel out of Egypt, described as an iron furnace.

easy.question: Who would not cross the Jordan?
answers: The Israelites
Moses
Joshua
easy.explanation: Moses said that he would not cross the Jordan, while the people would cross.

easy.question: What did Moses warn the people not to do?
answers: Build cities
Cross the Jordan
Forget the Lord’s covenant or make an image
easy.explanation: The people were warned to remember the covenant and avoid making an image.

medium.question: What would result from Moses not crossing the Jordan?
answers: Israel would cross and possess the land
Israel would return to Egypt
The land would remain uninhabited
medium.explanation: Moses would not cross, but Israel would cross and possess the good land.

medium.question: What does “a people of inheritance” mean in this context?
answers: A long journey
A people belonging specially to the Lord
A new law
medium.explanation: The phrase describes Israel as a people specially belonging to the Lord.

medium.question: What follows the description of Israel entering and possessing the land?
answers: A promise to return to Egypt
A command to build the tabernacle
A warning not to forget the covenant or make an image
medium.explanation: The passage follows the promise of the land with a warning against idolatry and covenant betrayal.

challenge.question: What central contrast appears in Moses’ words?
answers: Moses would die in the land, while Israel would cross the Jordan and possess it
Moses would cross, while Israel remained in the wilderness
Moses and Israel would return together to Egypt
challenge.explanation: Moses contrasts his own fate with Israel’s future crossing and possession of the land.

challenge.question: Why is the warning against making an image placed beside the covenant?
answers: An image was required to remember the covenant
Making an image could violate faithfulness to the covenant
Images were forbidden only in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: Idolatry is presented as a possible betrayal of the covenant with the Lord.

challenge.question: What do “a consuming fire” and “a jealous God” emphasize here?
answers: The Lord is unconcerned with human actions
The Lord guarantees that the land will always be hot
The Lord responds severely to covenant breaking and idolatry
challenge.explanation: These descriptions stress the seriousness of abandoning the covenant and worshiping images.

questions.question: What central contrast appears in Moses’ words?
answers: Moses would die in the land, while Israel would cross the Jordan and possess it
Moses would cross, while Israel remained in the wilderness
Moses and Israel would return together to Egypt
questions.explanation: Moses contrasts his own fate with Israel’s future crossing and possession of the land.

questions.question: Why is the warning against making an image placed beside the covenant?
answers: An image was required to remember the covenant
Making an image could violate faithfulness to the covenant
Images were forbidden only in the wilderness
questions.explanation: Idolatry is presented as a possible betrayal of the covenant with the Lord.

questions.question: What do “a consuming fire” and “a jealous God” emphasize here?
answers: The Lord is unconcerned with human actions
The Lord guarantees that the land will always be hot
The Lord responds severely to covenant breaking and idolatry
questions.explanation: These descriptions stress the seriousness of abandoning the covenant and worshiping images.

paragraphs.title: Decline, Exile, and Idolatry

easy.question: What would Israel do after living in the land for a long time?
answers: Make an image and do evil in the Lord’s sight
Build the Temple
Return to Egypt
easy.explanation: The passage says that Israel would corrupt themselves, make an image, and do evil.

easy.question: Whom did Moses call as witnesses?
answers: The priests and elders
Heaven and earth
The kings of the nations
easy.explanation: Moses called heaven and earth to witness against Israel.

easy.question: What would Israel serve after being scattered among the nations?
answers: The host of heaven
Israel’s prophets
Gods made by human hands
easy.explanation: They would serve gods made of wood and stone by human hands.

medium.question: Why would Israel not remain long in the land?
answers: Because they would make images and do evil before the Lord
Because there would not be enough rain
Because the land would be too small
medium.explanation: The passage connects idolatry and evil with losing the land.

medium.question: In “when ye shall have remained long in the land,” what does “remained long” mean?
answers: Leave the land immediately
Live in the land for a long time
Build walls in the land
medium.explanation: The phrase describes an extended period of living in the land.

medium.question: What sequence is described?
answers: Scattering, then making an image, then entering the land
Worshiping idols, entering the land, then scattering
Sin and image-making, loss of the land, then scattering
medium.explanation: The passage describes sin, followed by expulsion and scattering among the nations.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”?
answers: Only a small number would remain among the nations
All Israel would immediately return
The people would greatly increase in exile
challenge.explanation: “Few in number” describes a small remnant among the nations.

challenge.question: Why are the idols described as unable to see, hear, eat, or smell?
answers: To describe their beauty
To emphasize that they are lifeless and powerless
To teach how to make them
challenge.explanation: The missing senses show that the idols are human-made and unable to help anyone.

challenge.question: What contrast develops between the beginning and end of the passage?
answers: Israel crosses water and then crosses a wilderness
Israel worships the Lord in the land and later worships Israel in exile
Israel is ready to possess the land but may lose it and be scattered
challenge.explanation: Israel begins by preparing to possess the land but may lose it because of sin.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”?
answers: Only a small number would remain among the nations
All Israel would immediately return
The people would greatly increase in exile
questions.explanation: “Few in number” describes a small remnant among the nations.

questions.question: Why are the idols described as unable to see, hear, eat, or smell?
answers: To describe their beauty
To emphasize that they are lifeless and powerless
To teach how to make them
questions.explanation: The missing senses show that the idols are human-made and unable to help anyone.

questions.question: What contrast develops between the beginning and end of the passage?
answers: Israel crosses water and then crosses a wilderness
Israel worships the Lord in the land and later worships Israel in exile
Israel is ready to possess the land but may lose it and be scattered
questions.explanation: Israel begins by preparing to possess the land but may lose it because of sin.

paragraphs.title: Seeking the Lord and Returning Wholeheartedly

easy.question: Whom would the people seek?
answers: The Lord their God
The king of the land
Their brother
easy.explanation: The passage says they would seek the Lord their God.

easy.question: With what part of themselves were they to seek the Lord?
answers: With their eyes and hands
With all their heart and soul
With their feet alone
easy.explanation: They were to seek the Lord with all their heart and soul.

easy.question: What would a person do after turning back to the Lord?
answers: Build a new city
Leave the land
Obey his voice
easy.explanation: The passage says that those who turn to the Lord will obey his voice.

medium.question: What might cause someone to return to the Lord?
answers: Great success
Tribulation and trouble
A trip to another land
medium.explanation: The passage describes trouble followed by turning back to the Lord.

medium.question: What does “when thou art in tribulation” mean?
answers: When you are in distress
When you are very happy
When you are resting
medium.explanation: “Tribulation” means trouble, distress, or affliction.

medium.question: What sequence is described?
answers: Obeying first, then seeking the Lord
Being in trouble, turning to the Lord, and obeying his voice
Leaving the Lord and then becoming joyful
medium.explanation: The passage presents trouble, repentance, and obedience in that order.

challenge.question: What does “with all thy heart and with all thy soul” imply?
answers: Seeking the Lord should be wholehearted and sincere
The search should last only briefly
The Lord may be sought without seriousness
challenge.explanation: The repeated “all” emphasizes complete devotion.

challenge.question: What does the connection between “seek” and “find” teach?
answers: Seeking always fails
Sincere seeking of the Lord leads to finding him
There is no need to seek
challenge.explanation: The passage connects wholehearted seeking with finding the Lord.

challenge.question: Why is “in the latter days” important?
answers: It means the events happen only on one day
It refers only to nighttime
It points to a future time after a period of trouble
challenge.explanation: The phrase places the trouble and return to the Lord in a future period.

questions.question: What does “with all thy heart and with all thy soul” imply?
answers: Seeking the Lord should be wholehearted and sincere
The search should last only briefly
The Lord may be sought without seriousness
questions.explanation: The repeated “all” emphasizes complete devotion.

questions.question: What does the connection between “seek” and “find” teach?
answers: Seeking always fails
Sincere seeking of the Lord leads to finding him
There is no need to seek
questions.explanation: The passage connects wholehearted seeking with finding the Lord.

questions.question: Why is “in the latter days” important?
answers: It means the events happen only on one day
It refers only to nighttime
It points to a future time after a period of trouble
questions.explanation: The phrase places the trouble and return to the Lord in a future period.

paragraphs.title: A Merciful God Who Keeps His Covenant

easy.question: How is the Lord described?
answers: A merciful God
A powerful king
A vengeful judge
easy.explanation: The passage calls the Lord a merciful God.

easy.question: What will the Lord not forget?
answers: The people’s sins
The covenant with their fathers
The names of the kings
easy.explanation: The Lord will not forget the covenant he swore to their fathers.

easy.question: To whom did the Lord swear?
answers: Moses alone
All the kings of Israel
The fathers
easy.explanation: The verse refers to the oath sworn to the fathers.

medium.question: How is the Lord’s mercy connected with what follows?
answers: Because he is merciful, he will not forsake or destroy Israel
Because he is merciful, he will punish everyone
Because he is merciful, he will forget the covenant
medium.explanation: The passage presents mercy as the reason the Lord will not abandon or destroy his people.

medium.question: What does “he will not forsake thee” mean?
answers: He will not bless you
He will not abandon you
He will not remember you
medium.explanation: To forsake means to leave or abandon.

medium.question: What sequence of ideas appears in the verse?
answers: The Lord punishes, forgets, and then shows mercy
The Lord makes a covenant, destroys, and then abandons
The Lord is merciful, does not forsake or destroy, and remembers the covenant
medium.explanation: The verse begins with mercy and continues with promises of faithfulness.

challenge.question: What does the repeated “neither” emphasize?
answers: Several things the Lord will not do to his people
Several different nations
Several conditions for worship
challenge.explanation: The repetition lists several acts the Lord will not do: abandon, destroy, or forget.

challenge.question: Why mention the covenant with the fathers rather than only a promise to the present generation?
answers: To teach that the fathers were kings
To emphasize the Lord’s faithfulness to an earlier promise
To explain why Israel left Egypt
challenge.explanation: The reference shows that the Lord remembers and keeps his promises across generations.

challenge.question: What does the opening “for” explain?
answers: It introduces a question
It identifies a place
It explains why the Lord can be trusted
challenge.explanation: It connects the Lord’s mercy with his promise not to abandon or forget Israel.

questions.question: What does the repeated “neither” emphasize?
answers: Several things the Lord will not do to his people
Several different nations
Several conditions for worship
questions.explanation: The repetition lists several acts the Lord will not do: abandon, destroy, or forget.

questions.question: Why mention the covenant with the fathers rather than only a promise to the present generation?
answers: To teach that the fathers were kings
To emphasize the Lord’s faithfulness to an earlier promise
To explain why Israel left Egypt
questions.explanation: The reference shows that the Lord remembers and keeps his promises across generations.

questions.question: What does the opening “for” explain?
answers: It introduces a question
It identifies a place
It explains why the Lord can be trusted
questions.explanation: It connects the Lord’s mercy with his promise not to abandon or forget Israel.

paragraphs.title: Remember the Days of the Past

easy.question: What does the verse command people to do?
answers: Ask about and investigate the past
Build a new city
Count the stars
easy.explanation: The verse tells them to ask about the days that are past.

easy.question: From what point in history should they begin?
answers: The day of the Exodus
The day God created man on the earth
The days of King David
easy.explanation: The verse begins its comparison from the day God created man on earth.

easy.question: What does “from the one side of heaven unto the other” refer to?
answers: A small place on earth
One city
The whole expanse of heaven
easy.explanation: The phrase describes the entire span of heaven.

medium.question: Why does the verse direct people to examine all past days and the whole world?
answers: To discover whether anything so great and extraordinary had ever happened
